message.content:
Here’s a list of the long‑weekend holidays in Canada for 2023 (dates that fall on a weekday will create a long weekend by adding the nearest weekend days):

| Holiday | Date (2023) | Long‑Weekend Span |
|---------|-------------|-------------------|
| New Year’s Day | Jan 1 (Sunday) | Jan 1–2 (New Year’s Day + New Year’s Eve) |
| Family Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Ontario) | Feb 20 (Monday) | Feb 18–20 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Good Friday | Apr 7 (Friday) | Apr 7–9 (Friday–Sunday) |
| Victoria Day | May 22 (Monday) | May 20–22 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Canada Day | Jul 1 (Saturday) | Jul 1–3 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Labour Day | Sep 4 (Monday) | Sep 2–4 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Thanksgiving (Canada) | Oct 9 (Monday) | Oct 7–9 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Remembrance Day (Alberta, Saskatchewan, Manitoba, Ontario, Quebec) | Nov 11 (Monday) | Nov 9–11 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Christmas Day | Dec 25 (Monday) | Dec 23–25 (Saturday–Monday) |
| Boxing Day | Dec 26 (Tuesday) | Dec 24–26 (Saturday–Monday) |

**Note:**  
- Some provinces observe different holidays (e.g., Family Day in British Columbia is on the third Monday in February, not the second).  
- If a holiday falls on a weekend, the following Monday is often observed as a statutory holiday (e.g., New Year’s Day in 2023 was on Sunday, so Monday, Jan 2, is observed).  

Feel free to let me know if you’d like the list broken down by province or if you need additional details!
